newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond primary market sees busy day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond primary market sees busy day.

text.p: New issue activity dominated the U.S. corporate bond market today with prices on secondary paper moving generally in line with Treasuries, dealers said.

High-yield issuers, such as National Energy Group, Australis Holdings and Unison HealthCare Corp, kicked off what is expected to be a busy week of new issuance by selling at least $350 million in bonds in 144a private placement offerings.
Syndicate sources said the large amount of new supply forced at least one new issuer to increased the coupon on its deal.

Among international issuers, GTE North sold $250 million A1/AA rated debentures due 2008 through Morgan Stanley & Co; WMX Technologies Inc issued $200 million A1/A-plus rated notes due 1998 via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette; and Pohang Iron & Steel Co Ltd came to market with $300 million A2/A-plus rated 10-year notes through Salomon Brothers Inc.
In the secondary market, the Treasury rally pushed prices up 1/4 to 1/2 a point across the high-yield sector.
The rally in the Treasury market pushed the yield on the 30-year benchmark Treasury down to 6.68 percent, its lowest level since April.

Among selected issues, traders said Nextel Communications Inc bonds rose by a point and a half on Tuesday as the company held a meeting in Boston to show off its new wireless communications technology.
Spreads on TeleCommunications Inc. (TCI) bonds tightened by another five basis points on Tuesday, traders said.
TCI bonds began to make back some of their recent losses after the company announced on Monday that its free cash flow would move in the positive area for the first time in 1997.
